questions.passage: Regular reading strengthens vocabulary, improves concentration and helps readers understand ideas in context. Students who read a little every day often find it easier to organise their thoughts while speaking and writing. Reading does not have to be limited to textbooks; biographies, newspapers, stories and informative articles can all develop language and general knowledge.
questions.question: Answer the following: (a) Mention two benefits of regular reading. (b) What kinds of material can students read besides textbooks?
questions.model_answer: (a) Regular reading strengthens vocabulary and improves concentration; it also helps students organise their thoughts. (b) Students can read biographies, newspapers, stories and informative articles.

questions.passage: A village pond once served as the centre of community life. Over the years, people stopped maintaining it, and weeds covered much of the water. A group of students began cleaning the banks every Sunday. They also persuaded residents not to throw waste into the pond. Within months, birds returned and the water became clearer.
questions.question: Answer the following: (a) Why had the pond deteriorated? (b) What did the students do? (c) What change followed their efforts?
questions.model_answer: (a) The pond deteriorated because people stopped maintaining it and polluted it with waste. (b) The students cleaned the banks and persuaded residents not to throw waste into the pond. (c) Birds returned and the water became clearer.

questions.passage: Trees provide shade, reduce heat and support many forms of life. They also help protect soil and contribute to cleaner air. Planting trees is useful, but protecting mature trees is equally important because an established tree may take many years to replace. Communities can help by caring for local green spaces and preventing unnecessary cutting.
questions.question: State the main idea and give two supporting details from the passage.
questions.model_answer: The main idea is that trees are valuable to the environment and communities should protect them. They provide shade and reduce heat, support living organisms, protect soil and contribute to cleaner air. Mature trees are especially important because they take years to replace.

questions.passage: Meera arrived early for the examination. Instead of discussing her anxiety with other students, she quietly revised the points she had prepared. When the question paper was distributed, she read all the questions before beginning. This helped her manage her time and answer the easier questions first.
questions.question: What can you infer about Meera from the passage? Mention two qualities and support each with evidence.
questions.model_answer: Meera is prepared and disciplined. She revises quietly before the examination instead of wasting time. She is also organised because she reads the whole paper first and plans her time by answering easier questions first.

questions.passage: Water is often wasted through leaking taps, careless washing and unnecessary use in gardens. Small changes can reduce this waste. Repairing leaks, using a bucket instead of a running hose and reusing suitable household water for plants are simple measures. When many people adopt such habits, the total saving can be significant.
questions.question: What is the central message of the passage? Give two practical measures suggested by the writer.
questions.model_answer: The central message is that small changes in daily habits can significantly reduce water wastage. Two measures are repairing leaking taps and using a bucket instead of a continuously running hose. Suitable household water can also be reused for plants.

questions.passage: The library was nearly empty after school, but Arun visited it every afternoon. He did not always borrow a book. Sometimes he read newspapers, sometimes he searched for information for a project, and sometimes he simply sat quietly and read a story. Over time, his teachers noticed that his vocabulary and confidence had improved.
questions.question: Why was the library useful to Arun even when he did not borrow books? What improvement did his teachers notice?
questions.model_answer: The library gave Arun access to newspapers, information for projects and stories, so he could learn in different ways even without borrowing books. His teachers noticed improvement in his vocabulary and confidence.

questions.passage: Exercise is not only about physical strength. Regular activity can improve mood, sleep and concentration. Students can include simple activities such as walking, stretching, cycling or playing outdoor games. The aim is to develop a healthy routine that can be maintained over time.
questions.question: Write the main idea and two examples of activities mentioned in the passage.
questions.model_answer: The main idea is that regular exercise supports both physical and mental well-being and should become a sustainable habit. Two examples are walking and cycling; stretching and outdoor games are also mentioned.

questions.passage: When the school announced a science exhibition, many students initially hesitated because they thought successful projects required expensive equipment. Their teacher encouraged them to observe everyday problems and develop simple solutions. One group built a model to collect rainwater from a school roof. The project won appreciation because it was practical and easy to understand.
questions.question: Why did the students initially hesitate? Why was the rainwater project appreciated?
questions.model_answer: The students hesitated because they believed successful science projects required expensive equipment. The rainwater project was appreciated because it addressed a practical problem with a simple, understandable solution.

questions.passage: Good communication involves more than speaking clearly. A good listener pays attention, avoids interrupting and asks questions when something is unclear. Listening carefully can prevent misunderstandings and helps people respond appropriately. These habits are useful at school, at work and in everyday relationships.
questions.question: According to the passage, what are two habits of a good listener and why are they useful?
questions.model_answer: A good listener pays attention and avoids interrupting. Asking questions when something is unclear is another useful habit. These behaviours reduce misunderstandings and help people respond appropriately.

questions.passage: A local bus driver noticed that an elderly passenger often struggled to climb the steps. Instead of waiting for the passenger to ask for help, he began stopping a little closer to the pavement and waited patiently until the passenger was seated. Other passengers soon began offering similar help.
questions.question: What quality does the driver show? How did his behaviour influence other passengers?
questions.model_answer: The driver shows kindness, patience and consideration. He noticed the passenger's difficulty and helped without being asked. His example encouraged other passengers to offer similar assistance, showing how considerate behaviour can influence a community.

questions.question: Write an essay on 'The Importance of Reading for Students'. Include an introduction, benefits, practical reading habits and a conclusion.
questions.model_answer: Reading is one of the most useful habits a student can develop. It improves vocabulary, comprehension, concentration and general knowledge. Regular reading also helps students express their ideas clearly in speech and writing. Students need not read only textbooks; stories, newspapers, biographies and informative articles can make reading enjoyable. A practical habit is to read for a fixed period every day and note new words or important ideas. Thus, reading is both a source of knowledge and a way of developing confidence and communication skills.

questions.question: Write an essay on 'Protecting the Environment'. Mention individual responsibility, community action and a concluding appeal.
questions.model_answer: The environment supports every form of life, yet pollution, waste and careless use of natural resources are causing serious problems. Individuals can help by reducing waste, saving water and electricity, avoiding unnecessary plastic and planting or protecting trees. Communities can maintain clean public spaces, manage waste properly and encourage sustainable habits. Schools can also involve students in environmental projects. Protecting nature is not the responsibility of one group alone. If individuals and communities act responsibly, we can leave a healthier environment for future generations.

questions.question: Write a formal letter to the municipal authority requesting repair of damaged roads in your locality.
questions.model_answer:
To
The Municipal Commissioner
[City]

Subject: Request for repair of damaged roads in our locality

Sir/Madam,

I am a resident of [locality] and wish to draw your attention to the poor condition of the roads in our area. Several stretches have potholes and become difficult to use, especially during rainy weather. The condition is causing inconvenience to residents and may lead to accidents.

I request the municipal authorities to inspect the roads and arrange repairs at the earliest. Proper drainage and maintenance would also help prevent further damage.

Yours faithfully,
[Name]

questions.question: Write a letter to the editor of a newspaper about the need for better road safety awareness among students.
questions.model_answer:
To
The Editor
[Newspaper Name]
[City]

Subject: Need for greater road-safety awareness among students

Sir/Madam,

Through the columns of your newspaper, I wish to highlight the need for greater road-safety awareness among school students. Many young people cross roads carelessly, ignore signals or fail to use safe crossing points. Schools and local authorities can organise awareness programmes, demonstrations and talks on responsible road behaviour. Parents should also reinforce these habits at home.

I request you to highlight this issue so that schools, families and authorities work together to make roads safer for children.

Yours faithfully,
[Name]

questions.question: Write an essay on 'The Value of Time for Students'.
questions.model_answer: Time is one of the most valuable resources in a student's life because lost time cannot be recovered. Students who plan their day can balance study, rest, exercise and recreation. Regular work reduces last-minute stress and helps build discipline. Time management does not mean studying every minute; it means using available time wisely and avoiding unnecessary delay. Students should set realistic goals, follow a simple timetable and review their progress. Good use of time develops responsibility and helps students approach examinations with confidence.

questions.question: Write a letter to your school headmaster requesting permission to organise a reading club.
questions.model_answer:
To
The Headmaster/Headmistress
[School Name]

Subject: Request for permission to organise a reading club

Sir/Madam,

We, the students of Class X, request permission to start a reading club in our school. The club would encourage students to read stories, biographies, newspapers and other useful material. We propose to meet once a week under the guidance of a teacher and share books and reading experiences.

We believe the club will improve vocabulary, comprehension and confidence among students. Kindly grant us permission and allow us to use a suitable classroom or library space.

Yours obediently,
[Name]
Class X
